sessions.goal: Re-check the two-click confirmations (#345, #368): from the Nations screen (O) declare war on and denounce another nation, timing your second click; a second click up to 8 seconds after the first must confirm, not re-arm. Check the Nations list keeps its order while open, that a truce warning appears when war would break one, that L asks twice before you leave or disband, and that the command bar's buttons do not move under the cursor as pawns walk in and out of reach.
sessions.verdict: The #345/#368 confirmations work as intended. Second clicks at 6.3, 7.5 and 7.6 s confirmed and clicks at 8.6 and 11.1 s re-armed. The truce warning appears, L asks twice to both leave and disband, the Nations list holds its order while open (it re-sorts on reopen), and the fixed command-bar rows stay put. Still to fix: the pawn Talk/Gift/Invite buttons still hop between rows as different pawns come into reach, and a stale 'click again' prompt stays on screen after the confirm window expires. The diplomacy stage also loses your only village about 20 seconds in, while the HUD promises almost 5 minutes before sieges begin.

sessions.goal: Survive the first winter and keep your nation's people alive (#353). Found or join a nation early. Record whether the HUD warns when members go hungry or starve, whether Feed Residents appears and works when you carry food home, and count hunger deaths (events) over the winter; the 0.6.0 run on this seed saw 16 NPC hunger deaths across 7 nations with no warning.
sessions.verdict: The #353 fix works: in winter an amber HUD line ('Yellowton: N members hungry. Bring food home and Feed Residents.') shows everywhere, a 'Feed Residents (N hungry)' button appears in town when you carry food, and my nation lost no one. World hunger deaths fell from 16 to 5 over two thirds of the winter, but 4 of those 5 were AI nation leaders (two starved inside their own walls), which disbands nations. Feeding is click-heavy: each press gives one apple per pawn, so the warning comes back every ~12 game seconds, and the button moves around in the reflowing command bar.

sessions.goal: As a new player, try crafting and trading before and after founding a nation (#356, #354). Before you have a nation, the crafting screen must say the Workshop is locked until the Village era rather than telling you to build one. At a market, try Sell Resources in several situations (nothing to sell, your own stall only, merchants too poor) and record whether each refusal tells you why.
sessions.verdict: #356 is fixed: before a nation and in a Camp, the crafting screen says the Workshop unlocks in the Village era, and inside a town that has one it says every recipe is open. #354 is half done: when Sell Resources actually runs, its refusals are clear ('no stalls', 'No merchant here can pay: the richest has 0 coins, and your cheapest good (stone) sells for 18'). But the button greys out silently when you have nothing to sell, and it also greys out when you carry only food, apples or saplings, which the market does buy. Pawns grab every stall in your new camp so quickly that the player can't own one, so the 'only your own stall' refusal never came up.

sessions.goal: Audit the HUD at 960x540 inside a settlement (#350): enter your settlement and check that every box in the right-hand column fits on screen without overlapping the others or the command bar, that long lines wrap instead of being cut off, and that nothing important is lost in the compact layout. Also note any other text that is clipped, overlaps, or is unclear, with screenshots.
sessions.verdict: The #350 fix works for the right column: at 960x540 nothing runs off the bottom and long lines (status, settlement 'Next (K)', objective text) wrap well. But compaction cuts the wrong things: the player's Nation, Role and Land go while the 'PCIS' debug line stays, which hurts most inside someone else's settlement. The left column and centre have no such guard: expanding the Era box covers the command bar, and the inventory and tip overlap the buttons.

findings.title: Sell Resources is disabled when carrying only food/apples/saplings, though the market lists prices for them
findings.detail: With 5 chicken meat and no wood/stone, inside the Village of Greenham (Market Info shows 'Chicken Meat 57/51', 1 merchant), the Sell Resources button is greyed out and clicking it does nothing. The button's enable check only looks at wood/stone/planks/bricks, but the market itself (Market.isSoldInBulk) buys every non-coin, non-tool item, and the refusal text earlier even named 'sapling' as my cheapest good. Expected: the button is enabled for any sellable good, or explains why not.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/beyond-nations --seed 107; leave title, Start, Begin; pt walkto chicken; pt key e (x5 chickens); pt walkto stall 250; pt key e; click Sell Resources
alsoTitled: Purchase Food fails with 315 coins while the market lists apple prices

findings.title: AI nation leaders starve during winter: 4 of the 5 hunger deaths were nation leaders, 2 of them 'within the walls'
findings.detail: Over ticks 180000-219800 (winter day 1 and two thirds of day 2) the world logged 5 hunger deaths (pawn_death total=5), all in AI nations: Tina Brown, leader of Farmland (wilds, t206864, nation disbanded); Grace Lewis of Newport (wilds, t207460); Frank Taylor, leader of Blueport (within the walls, t212888); Bob Brown, leader of Westton (wilds, t214920); Wendy Walker, leader of Newport (within the walls, t218764). Down from 16 in the 0.6.0 run, but leaders are disproportionately the victims, and some starve inside their own settlement with markets around them. A leader death disbanded Farmland outright ('Tina Brown has died. Farmland has been disbanded.'). Expected AI leaders, who have coins and a market, to keep themselves fed, or at least not to make up 80% of the deaths.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/beyond-nations --seed 103 --season winter; Start, Begin; play ~40 min real time (tps ~15-30); grep PawnDeath out/events.jsonl

findings.title: Diplomacy stage: home village is captured ~20 game seconds in while the HUD says 'Sieges can begin in 4:58'
findings.detail: At tick 68 the HUD shows 'Sieges can begin in 4:58' while the Nations screen already says 'Your village: Besieged by Greenshire (2/6)!'. The siege went to 4/6 at tick 500 and at tick 1000 'Greenshire has captured your village! Upperwood has fallen ... You are without a nation.' In that time I had only opened the Nations screen (world paused), paid tribute, declared war (which broke the 60 s truce) and walked a few metres. Breaking the truce was my choice, but the player gets almost no time to react, and the 'Sieges can begin in' countdown contradicts a siege already in progress. Expected the countdown to hold, or not to be shown while a siege is running.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/beyond-nations --seed 111 --stage-diplomacy; space; click 480 315; click 480 315; read HUD + press o; (optionally tribute then War twice on Greenshire); Escape; walk ~20 s; pt events

Found a settlement or win a follower within 5 minutes, or your story ends.' and the HUD timer jumps back to 4:59 (it was at ~4:07 before I joined). findings.title: Command bar reflows when Feed Residents appears or disappears, so the next click lands on Talk/Build
findings.detail: The Feed button shows up in different places (297,414 in shots/c10.png; 115,414 in shots/c14.png) depending on which pawn buttons are present. When the last hungry pawn is fed it vanishes and 'Talk to Frank Robinson' slides into its spot (shots/fedagain.png). A second Feed click opened Phoebe Thompson's dialogue (t208124), and on another visit the rows shifted up and my 'Collect Stockpile' click built a Farm instead (t215560). The code comment on the button says it was put last 'so its coming and going moves nothing', but in play it does move things.

findings.title: Command bar: Talk/Gift/Invite buttons jump between rows depending on the nearest pawn's trait text length
findings.detail: The fixed buttons (Enter Settlement / Teleport Home / Plant Sapling row and Leave Nation) never moved as pawns came and went, which is the main fix working. But the pawn buttons still move: 'Talk to X (Stranger) - traits' is placed at the end of row 2 (x~386) when its text is short (Mia Brown - Gregarious; Dave Davies - Loyal, Greedy) and at the start of row 1 when long (Karl Smith - Loyal, Industrious; Irene Wilson - Greedy, Ambitious), and Gift/Invite slide between x=10 and x~386 to match. With the pointer parked at (470,476) the Talk button appeared and disappeared under it, and Gift (which spends coins) can take the spot where Talk was a moment earlier.
findings.repro: stage-diplomacy seed 111; join a nation (j); pt walkto pawn; pt move 470 476; take a screenshot every second as pawns wander in and out of reach

findings.title: Compact right column drops your own Nation/Role/Land and Region, worst inside a foreign settlement
findings.detail: Right column fits on screen in every case I saw (no box runs off the bottom, #350 holds). But in compact mode Player Info shows only the Energy bar, and Season shows only 'Spring - day 1/2, year 1' (Region and 'good farming and game' are lost). Inside a FOREIGN settlement (Upperland's village after Westerntown fell at tick 1000), Settlement Info names Upperland and its leader, so nothing on screen says you are now nationless; the code's rationale ('the settlement box already names the nation and leader') only holds in your own settlement. Expected Nation/Role kept when the settlement isn't yours, or the box expandable by click (clicking it does nothing).
findings.repro: pt start ... --stage-diplomacy; Start/Begin; H; E (enter home village); wait until it is captured at tick 1000

findings.title: Feed Residents gives each hungry pawn one item, so the same member is hungry again within ~600 ticks
findings.detail: With 50-60 apples in my pack, each press of 'Feed Residents (1 hungry)' handed the pawn one apple (+15 energy, while 'hungry' is under 80). The amber 'Yellowton: 1 member hungry' line and the button were back about 600 ticks (12 game seconds) later: fed at 216844, hungry again by 217424; fed 217464, hungry again by 218548. Keeping the nation fed meant standing in town pressing Feed every few game seconds. Expected one press to feed each pawn until it is no longer hungry (or to say 'still hungry' when it is not).
findings.repro: Found a nation and a settlement, carry apples (chop trees), stay inside the settlement in winter; press Feed Residents whenever it appears; pt wait 30 and watch it come back
